chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Hatam narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Ashj narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Malik ibn Zayd al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: I heard Ziyad ibn Aqala and Abdul Malik ibn Umayr narrating, from Jabir ibn Samurah, saying:

My father and I were with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and I heard him say: 'After me, there will be twelve leaders.' Then he lowered his voice, so I asked my father, and he said: 'He said: They are all from Quraysh.'

key_terms.أَبِي: My father (referring to the narrator's father in the chain)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number and lineage of his successors?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Khisal*, this hadith from Jabir ibn Samurah establishes the number and tribal origin of the twelve successors, serving as a primary proof for the Imamate of the Twelve Imams. The Prophet’s whispering of the specific names to his father highlights the esoteric nature of this designation, while the restriction to Quraysh underscores the political and genealogical legitimacy required for their leadership in early Islamic history.
